method.basis: Motor-related questions in eight registered C1 papers plus one dated October 2016 public copy. No general syllabus used to invent extra examinable motor requirements.
method.reading: All 42 complete available caption texts read, including optional/supplementary videos. Three original English archive transcripts replaced non-English default exports; one Dutch dubbed export required translation.
limitations: Not every C1 paper ever issued is available. Seven paper motor extracts readable; two older papers rely on the prior topic register.
Public copies/marking schemes are not authenticated originals. Unclear marks remain null; parent and child marks are not summed.
Caption-based review, not a full listening or frame-by-frame video inspection. A diagram not described in captions is unverified visually, not proven absent from every frame.

English evidence comes from original/default-audio metadata where available, supplied English ASR/manual tracks and English caption exports. No non-English-only lesson identified. Player language/dub preferences may select a different track.
A full-caption read is not the same as observing complete media when captions end early. No full copyrighted transcripts or original papers are redistributed.

Direct means the requested principle/procedure is taught; it does not mean every historical numeric variant appears verbatim. Partial includes dispersed ingredients, inference, missing qualification or incomplete integrated demonstration.
Evidence ranges are approximate navigation windows; caption timestamps can differ slightly between archived and current tracks.
No oral weighting or guaranteed grade is inferred. NVR is a circuit-completeness check, not claimed as a separately verified original question.

videos.title: Correct a Building’s Power Factor to a Chosen Target

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Power triangle, lagging/leading PF and a complete chosen-target kVAr calculation.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear analogy-to-example flow. The motor example calls 10 kW output but omits efficiency; use electrical input. Spoken/transcribed algebra contains slips: P=PF×S, Q=√(S²−P²). Billing comments are supplier-dependent.
videos.existingStudyNote: Use electrical input kW; convert shaft output through efficiency first.

videos.title: Three-Phase Power Factor Correction: From kVAr to a Star Capacitor Bank

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Revises a single-phase RL/capacitor example, then solves a three-phase delta load with star capacitors, including µF per phase.
videos.flowAndLimits: Systematic but assumes earlier circuit lessons. The single-phase revision corrects to unity; it does not work a non-unity target motor case. Keep single-phase and per-phase bank capacitances distinct.
videos.existingStudyNote: This example uses 600 V, 60 Hz and unity PF; the project uses 400 V, 50 Hz and 0.95.

videos.title: Capacitor-Bank Selection and Protection: A 200 kW Worked Example

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Chosen-target correction, bank steps, capacitor current and protection factors.
videos.flowAndLimits: Useful applied flow; substantial caption numerical noise. Existing note corrects the installed 125 kVAr versus calculated bank and rejects automatic savings in load kW or universal protection multipliers.
videos.existingStudyNote: The target needs about 110.6 kVAr. Size protection for the installed 125 kVAr bank (about 174 A at 415 V), using actual tolerance, harmonics, inrush and manufacturer data. Check switching steps at light load to avoid leading PF. Correction reduces upstream current and losses; the load’s working kW does not automatically fall.

videos.title: Overcurrent Relays: Pickup, Time Delay and Circuit-Breaker Tripping

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: CT–overcurrent-relay–breaker chain; pickup, inverse/definite/instantaneous timing and selectivity.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear functional animation. Network-scale examples transfer to LV principles. This is not a complete motor setting/coordination exercise or permission to disconnect a live CT secondary.
videos.existingStudyNote: The CT–relay–breaker principle also applies at low voltage. This is a functional introduction, not a relay-testing procedure. Never open an energised CT secondary; testing requires approved isolation and shorting arrangements.

videos.title: Thermal Overload Relays: Motor Current, Trip Contacts and Reset

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Overload causes, time delay, 95–96/97–98, contactor operation, reset and contact checks.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good concept-to-schematic-to-test progression; includes jamming, misalignment, bearings, ventilation and phase loss. One non-tripped/tripped wording slip conflicts with its correct demonstration; contact checks do not calibrate thermal operation.
videos.existingStudyNote: Normally 95–96 is closed; a trip opens it and closes 97–98. Contact checks do not establish thermal calibration. The relay needs coordinated short-circuit protection. Study detailed starter wiring after motor principles.

videos.title: Motor-Protection Circuit Breakers: Thermal, Magnetic and Phase-Loss Mechanisms

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Animated magnetic short-circuit, bimetal overload and differential phase-loss trip mechanisms.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good internal-mechanism flow. Explicitly acknowledges low-current phase loss may not trip. Features and thresholds belong to this design, not every MPCB.
videos.existingStudyNote: This mechanism is one MPCB design, not a universal feature list. Phase-loss sensitivity is not separate voltage monitoring. Select the current range and short-circuit coordination from the motor nameplate, starting duty and manufacturer data.

videos.title: Phase-Monitoring Relays: Phase Failure, Sequence and Voltage Conditions

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Phase loss/sequence, voltage imbalance, over/undervoltage, delay/reset settings and contactor output.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear functional introduction, then one product example. Check the actual model; relay output switches the control circuit, not motor fault current.
videos.existingStudyNote: Functions and thresholds vary by model. The output controls a contactor; it does not interrupt motor fault current. Keep the protective contact effective in every energising path, including while Start is held. Detailed motor wiring follows later.

videos.title: Induction Motors: Rotating Field, Rotor and Slip

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Stator/rotor, rotating field, induced rotor current, squirrel cage, slip concept, terminal star/delta and line/phase examples.
videos.flowAndLimits: Strong visual-concept sequence. Does not supply the numerical slip/synchronous-speed formula or wound-rotor resistance starting; separate lessons are necessary.

videos.title: How to read a Motor Nameplate (IEC standard)

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: IEC nameplate example: shaft kW, voltage/connection, full-load current, frequency, PF, speed/poles, efficiency, IP, insulation and duty.
videos.flowAndLimits: Orderly factor-by-factor explanation. Service factor is oversimplified as a percentage-current allowance; use the specific manufacturer data. Original English ASR archive reviewed, not only the Arabic export.

videos.title: Three-Phase Motor Power Factor — Worked Example

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Worked three-phase PF from electrical input power, voltage and line current.
videos.flowAndLimits: Short, focused arithmetic. Apparent power is VA, although the presentation calls it watts. PF and efficiency must remain separate.
videos.existingStudyNote: Use electrical input kW and apparent power in VA; efficiency is a separate ratio.

videos.title: Find the Line Current Needed for a Three-Phase Motor

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Worked line current from three-phase input kW, line voltage and PF.
videos.flowAndLimits: Short follow-on example. Apparent power is kVA, not kW; shaft-output data would additionally require efficiency.
videos.existingStudyNote: 25 kW is input power; 31.25 kVA is apparent power.

videos.title: Motor Output, Efficiency, Power Factor and Three-Phase Line Current

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Shaft hp→watts→electrical input through efficiency→apparent power→line current; identifies losses.
videos.flowAndLimits: Complete relevant chain. Complex-power notation is more demanding than C1 needs, but its scalar results are directly applicable. US supply values are example givens.
videos.existingStudyNote: Electrical input = Pshaft/η; apparent power = electrical input/PF.

videos.title: Induction-Motor Speed, Slip and Rotor Frequency: Six Worked Examples

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Six examples of synchronous speed, pole count, slip speed, per-unit/percent slip, rotor frequency and frequency changes.
videos.flowAndLimits: Strong, repetitive calculation flow. Approximate pole identification uses the nearest physically plausible synchronous speed; do not replace Ns with loaded rotor speed in the defining formula.

videos.title: Induction-Motor Torque and Speed: From the Rotating Field to the Load Curve

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Induction/force foundation, locked-rotor/pull-up/breakdown torque, load intersection, speed change and stalling.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good foundation before the longer torque–slip lecture. Final NEMA designs are examples. No external rotor-resistance starting demonstration.
videos.existingStudyNote: The final NEMA classifications are US examples; the torque–speed principles apply generally.

videos.title: How to Connect Motor Windings in Star and Delta

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Finding winding pairs, star/delta links, six leads, resistance balance and swapping two supply lines.
videos.flowAndLimits: Useful bench demonstration. Continuity identifies pairs, not start/end polarity by itself; nameplate voltage and manufacturer terminal diagram remain necessary.
videos.existingStudyNote: On 400 V: 230/400 V Δ/Y → star; 400/690 V Δ/Y → delta.

videos.title: Single-Phase Motors: Capacitor Start, Capacitor Run and Reversal

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Run/start windings, capacitor-run, capacitor-start and two-capacitor motors, centrifugal switch, relative winding reversal and capacitor-related humming.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good component-to-circuit flow. Its general capacitor statement must not imply every single-phase motor uses one. It does not compare shaded-pole/resistance-split-phase starting torque and PF systematically.
videos.existingStudyNote: Terminal arrangements vary; follow the motor diagram.

videos.title: Wire and Test a Single-Phase Forward/Reverse Drum Switch

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Forward/off/reverse drum switch, contact testing, winding reversal, earthing and stopping before reversal.
videos.flowAndLimits: Methodical model-specific wiring. Existing note correctly requires proving capacitors discharged; waiting a stated number of seconds alone does not establish discharge.
videos.existingStudyNote: Isolate and prove capacitors discharged before touching terminals.

videos.title: DC Motors: Magnetic Force, Brushes and Commutation

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: PMDC construction, brushes, split commutator, armature current, torque and polarity reversal.
videos.flowAndLimits: Strong animated foundation for the commutator question. PMDC battery reversal must not be generalised to reversing both circuits of a wound-field motor.

videos.title: Reverse a Wound-Field DC Motor: Armature or Field Connections

languageEvidence.assessment: English original/default audio verified in YouTube metadata; full Dutch dubbed captions reviewed with translation

videos.teaches: Force-direction cases: reverse armature or field alone to reverse torque; reversing both retains direction.
videos.flowAndLimits: Directly relevant DC distinction. Full Dutch auto-dub caption export reviewed with translation; YouTube separately identifies English (US) original/default audio and an English ASR track. Not mislabelled an English-transcript reread.

videos.title: Stepper Motors: Winding Sequences, Steps and Position

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Pulse sequence, discrete angle, frequency/speed, direction, holding position, PM/VR/hybrid and drive sequences.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear but much deeper than the short paper comparison. Optional placement makes an examined concept easy to skip.

videos.title: Servo Motors: Command, Error and Position Feedback

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Servo command/error/feedback loop, encoder/resolver, AC/DC types and synchronous versus induction speed.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good feedback explanation. Synchronous speed comparison appears mid-lesson, not a complete wound-field synchronous-motor lesson. Removing power does not instantly stop the rotor; existing note corrects this.
videos.existingStudyNote: Removing power does not stop a rotating load instantly.

videos.title: Torque–Slip Curve: Load Changes, Stable Operation and Stalling

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Torque–slip curve, changing load, inertia, equilibrium, stability and stalling.
videos.flowAndLimits: Rigorous, long follow-on lecture; optional depth. Induction-motor oscillation is not evidence of synchronous-motor hunting coverage. No external rotor resistance explanation found.
videos.existingStudyNote: Illustrative torque ratios are not motor ratings; use manufacturer limits.

videos.title: Single Phase Contactor - Connections Explained, Application plus the Current in the Coil and Load

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Single-phase contactor coil/load separation, terminals, switching and measured currents.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good physical introduction. Uses a maintained switch and lighting load; it does not teach DOL holding/no-voltage release. Complete original English archive text reviewed instead of Dutch export.

videos.title: How Do Direct On Line Motor (DOL) Starters Work?

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: DOL contactor/thermal relay, full-voltage starting, coil voltage, overload adjustment and physical operation.
videos.flowAndLimits: Accessible introduction, but the explanation that motor reactance only appears after starting is misleading. High starting current concerns the locked-rotor/slip-dependent motor impedance. No universal 5 kW DOL cutoff or blanket above-FLC setting should be inferred.

videos.title: What is MPCB | MPCB Vs MCB | Motor Protection Circuit Breaker @the Electrical Guy

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: MCB versus MPCB: adjustable current range, operation, trip test and claimed phase-loss functions.
videos.flowAndLimits: Original English archive reviewed. Incorrectly implies a C40 MCB trips at 40 A; the time–current curve governs. Test button does not prove calibration. Phase-loss features are model-dependent; the Module 10 mechanism lesson is stronger.

videos.title: How to Select MCB and Overload Relay Size for a Motor

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Horsepower conversion, assumed three-phase current and example MCB/overload range selection.
videos.flowAndLimits: Easy arithmetic but weak selection method: omits efficiency for shaft kW, treats 125% and ±20% as general rules and restricts MCB types too broadly. Existing optional-comparison warning is necessary; not a definitive sizing lesson.
videos.existingStudyNote: Use nameplate current and manufacturer coordination; the 125% shortcut is not a general selection rule.

videos.title: Single-Phase Direct-On-Line Starter Wiring

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Physical single-phase DOL connections, coil, holding auxiliary, start, stop, overload trip/reset and CPC.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear equipment demonstration. Specific routing through three overload elements is product-dependent; not a universal single-phase wiring prescription. No explicit supply-loss/restart walkthrough.

videos.title: 3 Phase Direct Online Starter DOL Wiring Diagram Connections Explained

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Three-phase power path and 230 V control: stop/overload NC, start NO and parallel holding auxiliary.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear schematic-to-operation lesson. Good DOL drawing preparation; supply-loss/no-automatic-restart follows from the circuit but is not explicitly walked through.

videos.title: 3 Phase Direct Online Starter DOL Wiring and Connections Explained

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Three-phase DOL physical wiring, 230 V coil/neutral, holding, overload, reset and alternative coil voltages.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good practical companion to the previous diagram. No explicit power-failure/restart demonstration or universal numerical overload sizing rule.

videos.title: Reversing a Three-Phase Motor: Mechanical and Electrical Interlocks

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Two-phase swap, two reversing contactors, fault if both close and mechanical plus electrical interlocks.
videos.flowAndLimits: Strong explanation and manufacturer-kit demonstration. It teaches reversing interlocks, not the full timed star–delta control circuit. US NFPA/UL references are not Kenyan design rules.
videos.existingStudyNote: NFPA/UL references are US-specific; the phase-swapping and interlocking principles apply generally.

videos.title: Star–Delta Starting: Sequence and Interlocks

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Star/delta winding connections, three power contactors, timer transition and reduced starting current/torque.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear power-sequence animation. Complete start/stop/holding/overload/timer control schematic and explicit cross-interlock wiring are absent from captions. Caption text confuses 33% coil current with 33% line current; winding current is about 58% of direct-delta starting winding current.

videos.title: Autotransformer Starting: Tap Voltage, Line Current and Torque

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Autotransformer tap ratio, motor versus supply current, torque-squared relationship and open/closed transition.
videos.flowAndLimits: Well-sequenced alternative-starter explanation. Percent current compares starting conditions, not rated running current. Canadian code examples are local to that example; no galvanic isolation or automatic conductor-size reduction.
videos.existingStudyNote: A tapped common winding is introduced before the starter circuits. Canadian 600 V and code examples explain the principle; use local supply values, manufacturer coordination and applicable BS 7671/EPRA requirements for selection. An autotransformer provides no galvanic isolation; reduced starting current does not by itself justify smaller conductors.

videos.title: What is a Soft Starter? from AutomationDirect

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: SCR voltage ramp, inrush/mechanical stress, bypass and soft stop; distinguishes VFD speed control.
videos.flowAndLimits: Concise manufacturer overview with good comparison. Does not establish detailed starter selection/settings for a particular installation.

videos.title: Variable-Frequency Drives: From Rectifier to Motor Speed

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Rectifier, DC bus, inverter/PWM and varying frequency/voltage to change motor speed.
videos.flowAndLimits: Long foundations before the drive; clear power-stage progression. Simplified waveform/electron analogies are not a rigorous machine model. A diode front end alone cannot return regenerated energy to the mains.

videos.title: Four-Quadrant Drives: Motoring, Braking and Regeneration

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Four speed/torque quadrants, motoring/generation, DC-bus braking resistor and regenerative front end.
videos.flowAndLimits: Concise and directly answers the regenerative-drive distinction. An ordinary VFD is not automatically a mains-regenerative drive.

videos.title: 5 Types of Power Factor Correction — Capacitor Bank Locations

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Individual/group/central/combined/automatic capacitor placement, motor switching and self-excitation hazard.
videos.flowAndLimits: Useful comparison. It mistakenly names self-excited induction generation synchronous generation; the existing note corrects it. Not a detailed motor-bank single-line drawing exercise; keep capacitors off VFD outputs.
videos.existingStudyNote: Capacitors can cause self-excited induction generation; keep correction capacitors off VFD outputs.

videos.title: Phase-Failure Relay with a DOL Starter

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Phase-monitor relay supply and a DOL holding-branch wiring example.
videos.flowAndLimits: Useful only as the existing optional circuit critique: Start bypasses the monitoring contact while held. Do not copy it as a correct protective circuit or count it as gap closure.
videos.existingStudyNote: Protection can be bypassed while Start is held; do not copy this circuit.

videos.title: Testing Phase Sequence: Rotation, Instruments and Consistent Phase Identification

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Sequence, direction, phase indicators, swapping two lines, consistent identification and tester ratings.
videos.flowAndLimits: Strong explanation before the practical demonstration; recognises equipment-specific two-pole phase indication. It is not a complete motor commissioning procedure.

videos.title: How to use a phase rotation meter? 👷🏽‍♂️

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Practical phase rotation indication, lead identification and correcting reverse sequence.
videos.flowAndLimits: Useful equipment example with PPE/voltage-range discussion. Any wiring alteration still requires isolation; the clip is not the whole safe-isolation procedure.

videos.title: Single-Phasing Fault in a Three-Phase Motor

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Phase loss at rest versus running, fuse/contactor/conductor causes, heating, noise and phase-failure protection.
videos.flowAndLimits: Direct fault concept with clear examples. Numerical current multipliers and claims of all windings being overcurrent are not universal; no complete humming diagnosis.
videos.existingStudyNote: Current multipliers are illustrative, not universal relay settings.

videos.title: Isolated Motor Bench Tests: Winding Resistance and Insulation Resistance

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Disconnected bench motor: remove links, compare winding resistances, check to frame and winding-to-winding insulation.
videos.flowAndLimits: Clear progression showing why a continuity check is insufficient. >200 MΩ is this meter/example, not a universal pass threshold. Not a complete site isolation, discharge, refit and commissioning sequence.

videos.title: Synchronous Condensers: Reactive Power and Voltage Support

languageEvidence.assessment: English caption text reviewed; not a full audio listening test

videos.teaches: Unloaded synchronous machine, reactive-power production/absorption and voltage/PF support.
videos.flowAndLimits: Good short identification. Does not explicitly connect increased field excitation to leading stator current or teach hunting. Not complete overexcitation teaching.
